reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Third cesarean with preeclampsia with severe features, platelets falling to 88, enoxaparin 9.5 h before neuraxial, suspected accreta, a known difficult airway, and latex allergy in a room set with standard supplies.

asa.rationale: Preeclampsia with severe features and evolving HELLP picture, suspected placenta accreta spectrum, prior difficult airway, obesity; some would assign 4.

decision.recommendation: delay to stabilize, then deliver with an accreta capable team
decision.rationale: Delivery is indicated, but first: treat severe range BP, start magnesium, get the repeat CBC, wait out the enoxaparin window or plan GA with a difficult airway setup, and assemble blood and the accreta team. Proceeding at 0730 with a spinal is unsafe.

redFlags.finding: Preeclampsia with severe features, possible HELLP
redFlags.evidence: BP 162/106 and 158/108, headache unrelieved by acetaminophen, visual spots, RUQ pain, 3+ reflexes; Plt 88 (171 one week ago), AST 96, ALT 110, LDH 312, UPCR 0.6.
redFlags.implication: Seizure, stroke, and coagulopathy risk; platelets may keep falling.
redFlags.action: Notify OB and MFM, magnesium sulfate, acute antihypertensive (IV labetalol or hydralazine), repeat CBC before neuraxial.

redFlags.finding: Prophylactic enoxaparin 9.5 h before planned neuraxial
redFlags.evidence: Enoxaparin 40 mg 10/26 2200 per patient and PAT note; case 0730.
redFlags.implication: ASRA timing for prophylactic LMWH is 12 h before neuraxial puncture (earliest about 1000).
redFlags.action: Delay neuraxial until at least 12 h and a reassuring platelet count, or plan GA.

redFlags.implication: Neuraxial hematoma risk; trend matters more than one number.
redFlags.action: Await repeat CBC before any neuraxial decision.

redFlags.finding: Suspected placenta accreta spectrum without completed workup
redFlags.evidence: MFM US 10/19: loss of clear zone, lacunae, subplacental vascularity; MRI pending prior auth; MFM recommends accreta capable team, two large bore IVs, crossmatch.
redFlags.implication: Massive hemorrhage and possible cesarean hysterectomy.
redFlags.action: Two large bore IVs, arterial line, crossmatched blood and MTP readiness, cell saver, accreta team and GYN onc availability; only T&S and one 18 G now.

redFlags.evidence: 2019 GA: grade III, failed first attempt, bougie, SpO2 89%; now Mallampati III (was II), BMI 38, neck 41 cm, preeclampsia edema.
redFlags.implication: GA may be needed if neuraxial is not possible or hemorrhage occurs.
redFlags.action: Difficult airway cart, video laryngoscope, smaller ETT, awake technique available, aspiration prophylaxis.

redFlags.evidence: Hives worse with each exposure, banana and kiwi cross reactivity; allergy band not applied, room set with standard supplies.
redFlags.action: Latex free room and supplies, allergy band.

redFlags.evidence: Preeclampsia (avoid methylergonovine) and asthma (carboprost relatively contraindicated).
redFlags.implication: Atony management relies on oxytocin, TXA, misoprostol.
redFlags.action: Plan oxytocin first, TXA available, avoid methergine and use carboprost cautiously.
RhIG postpartum if infant Rh positive.

planItems.item: Neuraxial preferred once enoxaparin and platelet criteria are met; otherwise GA
Arterial line, two large bore IVs
Difficult airway plan with VL and backup devices
Magnesium; note it potentiates neuromuscular blockade
Cefazolin 2 g (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 min of incision
Postop magnesium monitoring; resume enoxaparin per ASRA timing after catheter removal
